title: S7 - Therapist web workspace
description: Weeks 13-14. Exit: a therapist can invite a patient, assign standard and custom exercises and review progress entirely in the browser, and what they publish runs unchanged in the Android app.
goal: Let therapists do all of their daily work comfortably on a large screen.
entry_criteria: Confirm owners and realistic capacity before starting.
Required predecessor deliverables are available or scheduled in dependency order.

exit_criteria.description: All sprint issues meet their acceptance criteria and completion evidence requirements.
exit_criteria.deferral_authority: User instruction: therapist and physical-device checks are deferred until after implementation and do not block engineering delivery.
exit_criteria.disposition: Engineering work is complete with local evidence. The phone run in this criterion is deferred; not a development blocker.

exit_criteria.description: In the browser, invite a patient, create a custom exercise and assign it. Run it in the Android app, then review the result and its charts back in the browser.
exit_criteria.deferral_authority: User instruction: therapist and physical-device checks are deferred until after implementation and do not block engineering delivery.
exit_criteria.disposition: Engineering work is complete with local evidence. The phone run in this criterion is deferred; not a development blocker.

demo: In the browser, invite a patient, create a custom exercise and assign it. Run it in the Android app, then review the result and its charts back in the browser.
risks: A web change that alters what patients download would affect the Android app; keep cross-app checks in every assignment change.
Charts can imply clinical conclusions; show only existing measures and keep the not-clinically-validated wording.

execution_plan.first_week: Work prerequisites first; review integration and design risks midweek.
execution_plan.second_week: Integrate, execute acceptance checks, fix defects and demonstrate the sprint outcome.
execution_plan.capacity_policy: Estimates are provisional; reserve approximately 20% of actual team capacity for integration and defects.

issues.title: Build the exercise assignment editor
issues.description: Make assigning an exercise faster and safer than on a phone, with the same rules and the same result for the patient.
issues.requirements: User request, 2026-11-05: web app for therapists and administrators, in TypeScript

functions.name: editPrescription
functions.description: Guide the therapist through exercise, side and focus, targets, timing and review.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: publishPrescription
functions.description: Publish a retry-safe, immutable version with publish_prescription.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: Follows the same steps as Android: exercise, side and focus, targets, timing, review. Wide screens show a live summary beside the form.
Both ends of RangeArc can be dragged, snapping to 5 degrees and staying at least 15 degrees apart. Typed fields remain the precise and accessible input.

Validation matches the server: range 0-180 with high more than 10 above low, repetitions 1-1000, minimum cycle 100-30000 ms, maximum above minimum and up to 300000 ms, peak hold 0-5000 ms, trunk lean 0-90 degrees.
Publishing is retry-safe, an edit creates a new immutable version, and a new exercise always gets a new assignment ID so it cannot replace another one.
The picker shows each exercise once at its latest version, and editing a plan pinned to an older version still works.
A test proves that a prescription published from the web downloads into the Android cache unchanged.

completion.reviewed_by: Claude engineering evidence review (not clinical approval)

issues.title: Add custom exercises to the web app
issues.description: Give therapists the same custom exercises as Android, plus a page to manage them, which there is room for on a large screen.
issues.requirements: User request, 2026-11-05: web app for therapists and administrators, in TypeScript

functions.name: createCustomExercise
functions.description: Create an exercise with a name, measured joint and instructions.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: manageCustomExercises
functions.description: List a therapist's exercises and remove them with a confirmation.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: Creating an exercise takes a name, one of the six joints, instructions and optional Filipino instructions, with the same limits as Android (120 and 4000 characters).
Creation is retry-safe, the new exercise is selected automatically, and the form shows the per-joint angle hint and the 2D camera limits.
A My exercises page lists and removes exercises. Removal needs a confirmation and leaves existing assignments and history in place.
Exercises owned by other therapists are never offered.
An exercise created on the web runs in the Android app unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.deferral_authority: User instruction: therapist and physical-device checks are deferred until after implementation and do not block engineering delivery.
acceptance_criteria.disposition: Android decodes the web-created exercise in an automated test. Running it on a physical phone is deferred; not a development blocker.

functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

functions.name: showProgressCharts
functions.description: Show interactive, animated charts with an accessible table alternative.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: Queries one patient at a time in 50-record keyset pages, with filters for exercise, side and dates.
Charts respond to hover and keyboard, draw in with motion that respects reduced-motion settings, and offer a table alternative for screen readers.
Series stay separated by exercise version, prescription, side, model and algorithm, as on Android, and are never merged.
Each session shows the targets prescribed at the time, and custom exercises show the therapist's name for them.
Limited or invalid tracking is labelled, and pages keep the wording that measurements are not clinically validated.
